issue_paraphrase: Case-insensitive label matchers, written with an inline PCRE case-insensitive flag, expose a literal prefix string through the public matching API that is not guaranteed to match the stored label text byte-for-byte. Downstream code that pre-filters label sets by comparing directly against that prefix (instead of running the full regex) therefore prunes away label names whose capitalization differs, so prefix-based label lookups and regex matching disagree on which labels match. After the fix, case-insensitive matchers no longer advertise a byte-wise prefix at all.
fix_summary: Matcher.Prefix() returns "" (no usable prefix) when the underlying regex has a case-insensitive prefix (m.re.caseInsensitivePrefix), so callers stop doing byte-wise prefix comparisons on patterns where that would be wrong; only case-sensitive prefixes are exposed. Doc comment updated to say 'byte-for-byte'.
notes: Leaf Go package; test compiles and runs in ~5s at 1 CPU after the toolchain is installed. No network needed at test time beyond the initial module fetch. Single golden test file model/labels/matcher_test.go; the failing subtest is the (?i)abc.+ case-insensitive one.

issue_paraphrase: Relabeling rules that deliberately configure an empty separator or an empty regex replacement lose those empty values whenever the configuration is serialized and loaded again, because the empty strings are treated as 'unset' and omitted. After a reload the rule silently falls back to the built-in defaults (a ';' separator and the '$1' replacement), so the same rule rewrites label names differently than before the reload even though the configuration file was not changed.
fix_summary: Removed `omitempty` from the yaml/json serialization directives of Config.Separator and Config.Replacement so explicit empty strings are written out and survive a round trip (and Regexp.MarshalYAML now emits nil only when the compiled regex is nil instead of when its string is empty).
notes: Leaf Go package; test runs in ~5s. The golden test also covers the JSON marshal/unmarshal path (TestRegexp_JSONUnmarshalThenMarshal) but only TestConfig_UnmarshalThenMarshal is needed to detect the regression. No network needed at test time.

issue_paraphrase: HTTP API endpoints that serve gzip- or deflate-compressed responses can advertise a Content-Length computed before the body was compressed. Clients that trust that header then read a truncated or over-long stream and fail with unexpected-EOF style errors when downloading the response. The problem occurs when a handler sets Content-Length itself and then the response goes through the internal compression layer: the size is only corrected at the moment the compressed writer is created, not when the handler actually writes headers or the body, so the stale length survives to the wire.
fix_summary: compressedResponseWriter gains removeContentLength() called from Write, WriteHeader and Close (only for zlib/gzip writers), so a handler-set Content-Length is stripped at the point the compressed body is actually produced instead of only at construction time; the constructor-time Del calls are removed.
notes: Leaf Go package; the golden test spins up an in-process httptest server and real client, no external network. ~10s to run. Companion tests TestCompressionHandler_PlainText/Gzip/Deflate exist. The failure mode is a client-side decode error ('unexpected EOF'), a clear symptom.

issue_paraphrase: The promtool TSDB dump command silently omits the earliest samples of histogram-typed metric series: when a series contains both ordinary numbers and histograms, the first histogram sample of every histogram series is consumed internally and never printed, so dumps of histogram series are incomplete with no error or warning. The same bug also makes the dump behave unpredictably when it meets a sample type it does not recognize instead of reporting it.
fix_summary: formatSeriesSet in cmd/promtool/tsdb.go replaces the three separate 'for it.Next() == ValX' loops (whose first Next() call in loop 2/3 advances past and drops the first histogram/float sample) with a single switch loop over Next() until ValNone, and returns an explicit error for unknown sample types.
notes: Test builds a real tsdb storage fixture in a temp dir via promqltest.LoadedStorage and runs promtool dump logic on it; ~15-20s to run. The companion test TestFormatSeriesSetRejectsUnknownSampleType covers the unknown-type error path. tsdb tests in cmd/promtool do not need node or rust. No external network at test time.
